extraction_notes.note: Both algorithms are written in the `pseudocode` package inside figure floats, which latex_facts does not parse into lines; I segmented them by hand, one algorithm_step per numbered item 1)-8), with the full pseudocode environment as the statement.

Figure captions (including the RFPI outer-loop description and the CISR restart rule), the run-time table and the Summary section, which only restates earlier findings, got no nodes; the table's content is carried by claims ClP17 and ClP18.

Replica and cavity results are stated in running text as derived formulas, not as results. I typed them as heuristic claims that contain their numbered equations, because the appendices derive them (proof nodes PP1-PP4).
These are empirical findings read off figures and a table. I made them claims with rigor numerical rather than remarks, since later text relies on them.
Appendix A derives (7) across two subsections. Following the continued-proof rule, it is one proof node per subsection, both proving ClP3, with PP2 -> PP1 uses.
The appendix derivations introduce notation (the 1RSB ansatz, cavity systems) inside the proof text. Per step rule 4 these are introduce_variable steps, not definition nodes.

nodes.name: Eq. (1): Sparse signal distribution
nodes.statement: P\left(x\right)=\left(1-\rho\right) \delta \left( x \right) + \rho \tilde{P} \left( x \right),
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.label: sparse

nodes.name: Eq. (2): 1-bit measurement
nodes.statement: \textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\mathrm{sign} \left( \textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$} \right),
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.label: measurement

nodes.name: Eq. (3): l1-norm recovery scheme
nodes.statement: \mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{x} } \left \{||\vm{x}||_1 \right \} \ {\rm subj. \ to} \ {\rm sign}\left (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x} \right )=\vm{y} \ {\rm and} \ ||\vm{x}||_2=\sqrt{N},
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.label: l1recovery

nodes.name: Eq. (4): Partition function
nodes.statement: Z\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right)=\int d \textrm{\boldmath $x$} \delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}\vert^{2}-N\right)e^{-\beta\vert\vert\textrm{\boldmath $x$}\vert\vert _{1}} \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left ( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0 )_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x})_\mu \right ) ,
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: eq:partition_func

nodes.name: Eq. (5): Replicated partition function (n-th power)
nodes.statement: &&Z^n \left(\beta; \vm{\Phi}, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right) = \int \prod_{a=1}^n \left (d \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a \delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\vert^{2}-N\right) \times e^{-\beta\vert\vert\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}\vert\vert _{1}} \right )\cr && \hspace*{4cm} \times \prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left ( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0 )_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right ),
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: eq:expansion

nodes.name: Eq. (6): Replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.statement: q_{ab}=q_{ba}=\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} \rho & (a=b=0) \cr m & (a=1,2,\ldots,n; \ b=0) \cr 1 & (a=b=1,2,\ldots,n) \cr q & (a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n) \end{array} \right . ,
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: RSanzats

nodes.name: Eq. (7): RS average free energy density
nodes.statement: \bar{f} &=& \mathop{\rm extr}_{\omega} \Biggr\{ \left[\phi \left(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0};\hat{Q}\right)\right]_{\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0},z} -\frac{1}{2}\hat{Q}+\frac{1}{2}\hat{q}\chi+\hat{m}m \nonumber\\ &&+\frac{\alpha}{2\pi\chi}\left(\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right )-\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}\right) \Biggr\}
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: eq:free energy

nodes.name: Eq. (8): Single-site cost phi
nodes.statement: \phi \left(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0};\hat{Q}\right) =\mathop{\rm min}_{x}\left\{ \frac{\hat{Q}}{2}x^2-\left(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0\right)x+\vert x \vert\right\}\nonumber\\ = -\frac{1}{2\hat{Q}}\left( \left \vert\sqrt{\hat{q}}z +\hat{m}\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right \vert-1\right)^2 \Theta \left (\left \vert\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right \vert-1 \right ).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method

nodes.name: Eq. (9): RS saddle point equations
nodes.statement: \hat{q}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi \chi^2} \left(\arctan \left(\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m}\right) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}\right), \\ \hat{m}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi\chi\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}, \\ \hat{Q}^{2}&=&2\left\{ \left(1-\rho\right)\left[\left(\hat{q}+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right) -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\hat{q}}} \right] \right . \nonumber\\ &&\left . +\rho\left[\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right) -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2\right)}}\right]\right\}, \\ \chi&=&\frac{2}{\hat{Q}}\left[\left(1-\rho\right) H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right)+\rho H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right)\right], \\ m&=&\frac{2\rho\hat{m}}{\hat{Q}}H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right),
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: results

nodes.name: Eq. (14): MSE in terms of m
nodes.statement: {\rm MSE}=\left [ \left |\frac{\hat{\vm{x}}}{|\hat{\vm{x}}|}-\frac{\vm{x}^0}{|\vm{x}^0|} \right |^2 \right ]_{\vm{\Phi,\vm{x}^0}} =2\left (1-\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho}} \right ).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: MSE

nodes.name: Eq. (15): AT stability condition
nodes.statement: &&\frac{\alpha}{\pi (\hat{Q}\chi)^2} \arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) \cr && \times 2\left ((1-\rho)H\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}} \right ) +\rho H\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}} \right ) \right ) -1<0,
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.label: AT

nodes.name: Eq. (16): Unconstrained min-max cost
nodes.statement: &&\mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{x},\vm{ z} > 0} \mathop{\rm max}_{\vm{a},\Lambda} \left \{ \sum_{i=1}^N |x_i|+\sum_{\mu=1}^M a_\mu \left (\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} x_i-z_\mu \right ) +\frac{\Lambda}{2}\left (\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^2-N \right ) \right \} \cr && = \mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{ x},\vm{ z} > 0} \mathop{\rm max}_{\vm{a},\Lambda} \left \{ \sum_{i=1}^N \left (\frac{\Lambda}{2} x_i^2 + |x_i| \right )-\sum_{\mu=1}^Ma_\mu z_{\mu} +\sum_{\mu,i} \Phi_{\mu i} a_\mu x_i -\frac{N\Lambda}{2} \right \},
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: coupled_cost

nodes.name: Eq. (17): Single-body cost for x_i
nodes.statement: {\cal L}_i(x_i)=\frac{A_i}{2} x_i^2-H_i x_i +|x_i|,
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: x_cost

nodes.name: Eq. (18): Single-body cost for (a_mu, z_mu)
nodes.statement: {\cal L}_\mu(a_\mu,z_\mu) =-\frac{B_\mu}{2}a_\mu^2+K_\mu a_\mu-z_\mu a_\mu,
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: mu_cost

nodes.name: Eq. (19): Cavity self-consistent equations
nodes.statement: K_\mu &=& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i-B \hat{a}_\mu, \\ \hat{a}_\mu &=& -\frac{1}{B} f^{\prime}\left (K_\mu \right ), \\ H_i &=& \sum_{\mu =1}^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \Gamma \hat{x}_i, \\ \hat{x}_i &=& \frac{1}{A} g^{\prime}\left (H_i \right ),
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: BPnaive1

nodes.name: Eq. (23): Onsager coefficient Gamma
nodes.statement: \Gamma=B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime} \left (K_\mu \right ) \right ) =B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M \Theta \left (|K_\mu | -1 \right ) \right ).
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: Gamma

nodes.name: Eq. (24): Equation for B
nodes.statement: B=A^{-1}\left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime} \left (H_i \right ) \right ) =A^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N \Theta \left (|H_i | -1\right ) \right ).
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: eq:B

nodes.name: Eq. (25): Modified update for a_mu
nodes.statement: \hat{a}_\mu &=& \hat{a}_\mu -\frac{1}{B} f^{\prime}\left (\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i \right ),
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: BPnaive2rev

nodes.name: Eq. (26): Averaged n-th moment of Z
nodes.statement: &&\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}= \int \prod_{a=1}^n \left (d \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\vert^{2}-N\right) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^{0}}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Zmoment

nodes.name: Eq. (27): Delta-function identity for q_ab
nodes.statement: 1=N \int dq_{ab} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Eq. (28): Replica joint distribution
nodes.statement: &&P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )= \frac{1}{V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) } P(\vm{x}^0) \times \prod_{a=1}^n \left (\delta \left (\left |\vm{x}^a\right |^2 -N \right ) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \prod_{a>b} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: replica_joint_dist

nodes.name: Eq. (29): Z^n as integral over Q
nodes.statement: \left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}} =\int d\vm{Q} \left (V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \times \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Zn

nodes.name: Eq. (30): Definition of Xi(Q)
nodes.statement: \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) =\int \prod_{a=0}^n d\vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q} \right ) \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Xi

nodes.name: Eq. (31): Covariance of u
nodes.statement: \left [u_\mu^a u_\nu^b \right ]_{\vm{\Phi},\{\vm{x}^a\}} =\delta_{\mu \nu} q_{ab},
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Eq. (32): Gaussian evaluation of Xi
nodes.statement: \Xi(\vm{Q}) &=&\left (\frac{\int d \vm{u} \exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^0 u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M \cr &=& \left (2 \int \frac{ d \vm{u}\exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \Theta\left (u^0 \right )\prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: logXi

nodes.name: Eq. (33): Fourier representation of norm delta
nodes.statement: \delta\left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) =\frac{1}{4 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{aa} \exp \left (-\frac{1}{2} \hat{q}_{aa} \left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) \right )
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Eq. (34): Fourier representation of overlap delta
nodes.statement: \delta\left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b -N q_{ab}\right ) =\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{ab} \exp \left ( \hat{q}_{ab} \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b-N q_{ab} \right ) \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Eq. (35): Saddle point expression of ln V
nodes.statement: &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q}) =\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{\vm{Q}}} \left \{ -\frac{1}{2} {\rm Tr} \hat{\vm{Q}}\vm{Q} \right . \cr && \hspace*{2cm} \left . + \ln \left ( \int d\vm{x} P(x^0) \exp \left (\frac{1}{2} \vm{x}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{Q} }\vm{x}-\beta \sum_{a=1}^n \beta |x^a| \right ) \right ) \right \}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: logV

nodes.name: Eq. (36): RS ansatz for conjugate variables
nodes.statement: \hat{q}_{ab}=\hat{q}_{ba} =\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} 0, &( \mbox{$a=b=0$})\\ \hat{m}, &( \mbox{$a=1,2,\ldots,n$; $b=0$})\\ \hat{Q}, &( \mbox{$a=b=1,2,\ldots,n$})\\ \hat{q}, &( \mbox{$a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n$}) \end{array} \right . .
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: RShatQ

nodes.name: Eq. (37): Gaussian parametrization of u under RS
nodes.statement: && u^0=\sqrt{\rho-\frac{m^2}{q}}s^0 + \frac{m}{\sqrt{q}} z, \\ && u^a=\sqrt{1-q} s^a+ \sqrt{q} z, \ (a=1,2,\ldots,n)
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: Newgauss0

nodes.name: Eq. (39): RS expression of Xi
nodes.statement: \Xi(\vm{Q})=\left ( 2 \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) H^n \left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \right )^M.
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: NewXi

nodes.name: Eq. (40): Hubbard-Stratonovich identity
nodes.statement: \exp \left (\hat{q} \sum_{a>b(\ge 1)} x^a x^b \right )=\int {\rm D}z \exp \left (\sum_{a=1}^n \left ( -\frac{\hat{q}}{2} (x^a)^2 + \sqrt{\hat{q}} z x^a \right ) \right )
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Eq. (41): RS expression of ln V
nodes.statement: &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q} )=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{Q}, \hat{q},\hat{m} } \left \{ \frac{n}{2}\hat{Q}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \hat{q}q -\hat{m} m \right . \cr &&\left . +\ln \left [\left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q} \!+\! \hat{q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\!\beta |x| \right ) \right )^n \right ]_{x^0,z} \right \}.
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: NewV

nodes.name: Eq. (42): Asymptotic form of energy term
nodes.statement: &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) \ln H\left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \cr &&=\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho -m^2} }z \right )\left (-\frac{z^2}{2\chi} \Theta(z) \right ) \cr &&= -\frac{1}{4 \pi \chi}\left (\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2} \right )
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Eq. (43): Asymptotic form of entropy term
nodes.statement: &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta} \ln \left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left (\beta \left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\! |x| \right ) \right ) \right ) \cr && =-\phi\left (\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0;\hat{Q} \right ).
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Eq. (44): 1RSB free energy
nodes.statement: &&\overline{f}=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\omega}\left \{ -\frac{1}{\beta } \left [ \ln \left (\int {\rm D}{t} \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_0 \right ) \right ) \right ]_{x^0,z} \right . \cr && \hspace*{0cm}-\frac{1}{2\beta}(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)+\frac{\hat{q}_1}{2\beta} (1-q_1)+\frac{p}{2\beta} (\hat{q}_1q_1-\hat{q}_0q_0 )+\frac{1}{\beta}\hat{m}m\cr && \hspace*{0cm}\left . -\frac{2\alpha}{\beta p}\! \int \! {\rm D}z H\left (\!\frac{m }{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z\! \right ) \ln \left (\int {\rm D}t \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_1 \right ) \right ) \right \},
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: 1RSB

nodes.name: Eq. (45): Linearized equation for q1-q0
nodes.statement: &&q_1-q_0=\left [ \frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )^2} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right . \cr &&\hspace*{4cm} \left . - \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t^2}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} -\left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right )\right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0) \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0)
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution

nodes.name: Compressed sensing (CS)
nodes.statement: \textit{Compressed (or compressive) sensing} (CS) is a technique for recovering a high-dimensional signal from lower-dimensional data, whose components represent partial information about the signal, by utilizing prior knowledge on the sparsity of the signal \cite{CandesWakin2008}.

nodes.statement: Addressing the practical relevance of CS in such operation, Boufounos and Baraniuk recently proposed and examined a CS scheme, often called {\em 1-bit compressed sensing (1-bit CS)}, in which the signal is recovered from only the sign data of the linear measurements $\textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\mathrm{sign}\left(\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$}\right)$, where $\mathrm{sign}(x)=x/|x|$ for $x \ne 0$ operates for vectors in the component-wise manner \cite{1bitCS}.

nodes.name: Renormalized Fixed Point Iteration (RFPI)
nodes.statement:
\begin{pseudocode}[ruled]{Renormalized Fixed Point Iteration}{\delta,\lambda}
1)\ \mbox{\bf Initialization}:\\
 \hspace{15pt}\text{Seed}: \hspace{80pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\ \text{s.t}\ ||\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}||_{2}=\sqrt{N},\\
 \hspace{15pt}\text{Descent step size}:\hspace{13pt}\delta\\
\hspace{15pt}\text{Counter}: \hspace{62pt} k\GETS 0\\

2)\ \mbox{\bf Counter\ Increase}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}k \GETS k+1\\

3)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient}:\\
\hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}\GETS  (\textsc{Y}\Phi)^{\rm T} f^\prime (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1})\\

4)\ \mbox{\bf Gradient projection on sphere surface}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\GETS \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}-\langle \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k},
 \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}\rangle\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}/N\\

5)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{h}\GETS \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}-\delta\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\\

6)\ \mbox{\bf Shrinkage ($l_1$-gradient descent)}:\\ 
 \hspace{30pt}(\mathbf{u})_i\GETS\text{sign}((\mathbf{h})_{i})\text{max}\{|(\mathbf{h})_i|-\frac{\delta}{\lambda},0\} \ \text{for all}\ i \\

7)\ \mbox{\bf Normalization}:\\
\hspace{30pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k}\GETS \sqrt{N} \frac{\mathbf{u}}{||\mathbf{u}||_2}\\

8)\ \bold{Iteration}: \mbox{Repeat from 2) until convergence.}
\end{pseudocode}

nodes.statement_short: Inner loop of RFPI: one-sided quadratic gradient step projected on the sphere, soft-thresholding shrinkage, then renormalization to $\sqrt N$, repeated until convergence.

nodes.name: RS saddle point equations
nodes.statement:
The extremization problem of (\ref{eq:free energy}) yields the following saddle point equations: 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hat{q}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi \chi^2} \left(\arctan \left(\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m}\right) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}\right), \\
\hat{m}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi\chi\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}, \\
\hat{Q}^{2}&=&2\left\{ \left(1-\rho\right)\left[\left(\hat{q}+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right)
          -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\hat{q}}} \right] \right . \nonumber\\
          &&\left . +\rho\left[\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right)
          -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2\right)}}\right]\right\}, \\
\chi&=&\frac{2}{\hat{Q}}\left[\left(1-\rho\right)
H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right)+\rho H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right)\right], \\
m&=&\frac{2\rho\hat{m}}{\hat{Q}}H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right), \end{eqnarray}
where $H(x)=\int_x^{+\infty} {\rm D}z$.

nodes.name: Cavity-inspired Signal Recovery (CISR), inner loop
nodes.statement:
\begin{pseudocode}[ruled]{Cavity-inspired Signal Recovery}{\textsc{B}, \mathbf{x}^*, \mathbf{H}^*}

1)\ \mbox{\bf Initialization}:\\
 \hspace{15pt}\text{X seed}: \hspace{65pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0} \GETS \hat{\mathbf{x}}^*\\
 \hspace{15pt}\text{H seed}: \hspace{65pt} \mathbf{H}_0 \GETS \mathbf{H}^* \\
\hspace{15pt}\text{Counter}: \hspace{62pt} k\GETS 0\\

2)\ \mbox{\bf Counter increase}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}k \GETS k+1\\

3)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent}:\\

 \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{H}_{k}\GETS  \mathbf{H}_{k-1}-\textsc{B}^{-1}(\textsc{Y}\Phi)^{\rm T} 
 f^\prime\left (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} \right ) \\

4)\ \mbox{\bf Assessment of Onsager coefficient}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}
 \Gamma \GETS (\textsc{NB})^{-1} \vm{1}^{\rm T} f^{\prime\prime} \left (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} \right )\\

5)\ \mbox{\bf{Self-feedback \ cancellation}}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_k \GETS \mathbf{H}_{k}+\Gamma \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}\\

6)\ \mbox{\bf Shrinkage ($l_1$-gradient descent)}:\\ 
 \hspace{30pt}(\mathbf{u})_i\GETS\text{sign}((\tilde{\mathbf{H}})_{i})
 \text{max}\{|(\tilde{\mathbf{H}})_i|-1,0\} \  \text{for all}\ i\\

7)\ \mbox{\bf Normalization}:\\
 \hspace{30pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k}\GETS \sqrt{N} \frac{\mathbf{u}}{||\mathbf{u}||_2}\\

8)\ \bold{Iteration}: \mbox{Repeat from 2) until convergence.}
\end{pseudocode}

nodes.name: CISR outer loop (control of B)
nodes.statement: In practice, the initial value of $B$ should be set so that only a single entry becomes nonzero. This is easily done by the Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding algorithm \cite{BIHT}, which requires the number of nonzero entries as extra prior knowledge. After the initial value is set, $B$ is reduced as $B_n=r B_{n-1}$ with an appropriate constant $0<r < 1$, where $n$ is the counter of the outer loop. The algorithm terminates when the difference between the convergent solutions of two successive outer loops is sufficiently small.

nodes.name: Comparison of CISR with RFPI
nodes.statement: The resultant algorithm is somewhat similar to RFPI as the combination of (\ref{BPnaive3}) and (\ref{BPnaive2rev}) roughly acts as the {\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent} step in Figure \ref{RFPI}. However, as the length of $\vm{H}=(H_i)=\vm{\Phi}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{a}}$ is not restricted to a fixed value, the current algorithm does not need a small step size $\delta$ for the convergence. Another significant difference from RFPI is the existence of the Onsager reaction term in (\ref{BPnaive3}). This term effectively cancels the self-feedback effects included in $H_i$ of (\ref{BPnaive3}), and this is expected to accelerate the convergence of the algorithm.

nodes.statement_short: CISR resembles RFPI but needs no small step size since $H$ is unnormalized, and its Onsager term cancels self-feedback, expected to speed convergence.

nodes.statement:
The MSE results obtained in numerical experiments with the cavity-inspired signal recovery (CISR) algorithm are shown in Figures \ref{fig:BPMSE} (a)--(d). They indicate that except in the case in which the nonzero density $\rho$ of the original signals is significantly low, 
CISR provides MSE values almost equal to or lower than those of RFPI.

nodes.name: CISR yields sparser signals than RFPI
nodes.statement: The FN probabilities for CISR are higher than those for RFPI, while the FP probabilities are lower. This implies that CISR has a capability of yielding sparser signals than RFPI, which is presumably because parameter $B$ of CISR is initially set so that only a single entry of $\hat{\vm{x}}$ is nonzero while such a tuning is not taken into account in RFPI.

conclusions: The FN probabilities for CISR are higher than those for RFPI, while the FP probabilities are lower

nodes.name: CISR is hundreds of times faster than RFPI
nodes.statement: Although the run times of RFPI may be reduced by optimally tuning the descent step size $\delta$, CISR is several hundreds of times faster than RFPI.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
conclusions: CISR is several hundreds of times faster than RFPI

nodes.name: Onsager reaction term speeds up CISR convergence
nodes.statement: The NORT values in Table \ref{table1} are the run times when the Onsager reaction term in (\ref{BPnaive3}) was removed from CISR. Their being 1.13--2.37 times longer than those for CISR indicates that the cancellation of the self-feedback effects by adding the Onsager reaction term speeds the convergence of CISR significantly.

conclusions: the cancellation of the self-feedback effects by adding the Onsager reaction term speeds the convergence of CISR significantly

nodes.name: Derivation of (7), part 2: RS ansatz and zero-temperature limit
nodes.statement:
Let us assume that the relevant saddle point in assessing (\ref{Zn}) is of the form of (\ref{RSanzats}) and, accordingly, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\hat{q}_{ab}=\hat{q}_{ba} =\left \{
\begin{array}{ll}
0, &( \mbox{$a=b=0$})\\
\hat{m}, &( \mbox{$a=1,2,\ldots,n$; $b=0$})\\
\hat{Q}, &( \mbox{$a=b=1,2,\ldots,n$})\\
\hat{q}, &( \mbox{$a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n$})
\end{array}
\right .  . \end{eqnarray}
$n+1$ dimensional Gaussian random variables $u^0,u^1,\ldots u^n$ whose variance and covariance are provided as (\ref{RSanzats}) can be expressed as 
\begin{eqnarray}
&& u^0=\sqrt{\rho-\frac{m^2}{q}}s^0 + \frac{m}{\sqrt{q}} z, \\
&& u^a=\sqrt{1-q} s^a+ \sqrt{q} z, \ (a=1,2,\ldots,n) \end{eqnarray}
utilizing $n+2$ independent standard Gaussian random variables $z$ and $s^0,s^1,\ldots,s^n$. This indicates that (\ref{logXi}) is evaluated as
\begin{eqnarray}
\Xi(\vm{Q})=\left (
2 \int {\rm D}z 
H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right )
H^n \left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \right )^M. \end{eqnarray}
On the other hand, substituting (\ref{RShatQ}) into (\ref{logV}), in conjunction with the identity
\begin{eqnarray}
\exp \left (\hat{q} \sum_{a>b(\ge 1)} x^a x^b \right )=\int {\rm D}z \exp \left (\sum_{a=1}^n 
\left (
-\frac{\hat{q}}{2} (x^a)^2 + \sqrt{\hat{q}} z x^a \right ) \right ) 
\end{eqnarray}
provides 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q} )=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{Q}, \hat{q},\hat{m} }
\left \{
\frac{n}{2}\hat{Q}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \hat{q}q -\hat{m} m \right . \cr
&&\left . 
+\ln 
\left [\left (
\!
\int 
\!
dx \exp 
\!\left (
\!
-\frac{\hat{Q}
\!+\! \hat{q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right )
\!x \!-\!\beta |x| \right )
\right )^n \right ]_{x^0,z} \right \}. \end{eqnarray}
Although we have assumed that $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expressions of (\ref{NewXi}) and (\ref{NewV}) are likely to hold for $n \in \mathbb{R}$ as well. Therefore the average free energy $\overline{f}$ can be evaluated by substituting these expressions into the formula $\overline{f}= -\lim_{n\to 0} (\partial/\partial n) \left ((\beta N)^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n (\beta; \vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0 ) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0} \right )$. 

In the limit of $\beta \to \infty$, a nontrivial saddle point is obtained only when $\chi \equiv \beta (1-q)$ is kept finite. Accordingly, we change the notations of the auxiliary variables as $\hat{Q}+\hat{q} \to \beta \hat{Q}$, $\hat{q} \to \beta^2 \hat{q}$, and $\hat{m} \to \beta \hat{m}$. Furthermore, we use the asymptotic forms
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}\int {\rm D}z
H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right )
\ln H\left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \cr
&&=\int {\rm D}z
H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho -m^2} }z \right )\left (-\frac{z^2}{2\chi} \Theta(z) \right ) \cr
&&= -\frac{1}{4 \pi \chi}\left (\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right )
-\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2} \right ) 
\end{eqnarray}
and 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}
\ln 
\left (
\!
\int 
\!
dx \exp 
\!\left (\beta \left (
\!
-\frac{\hat{Q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right )
\!x \!-\! |x| \right ) \right )
\right ) \cr
&& =-\phi\left (\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0;\hat{Q} \right ). 
\end{eqnarray}
Using these in the resultant expression of $\overline{f}$ offers (\ref{eq:free energy}).

nodes.name: Cavity fields equal full fields
nodes.statement:
Equations (\ref{VstepH}) and (\ref{RstepH}) indicate the difference between 

$H_{i \to \mu }$ and $H_{i}$ 

is vanishingly small for $N \to \infty$ as $\Phi_{\mu i}$ scales as $O\left (N^{-1/2} \right )$, and similarly for 

$K_{\mu \to i}$ and $K_\mu$. 

This also allows us to handle $A_i$ and $A_{i \to \mu}$ as a single site-independent parameter $A$, and we similarly deal with $B_\mu $ and $B_{\mu \to i}$ as $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $\Phi_{\mu i}=O(N^{-1/2})$, cavity and full quantities coincide and $A$, $B$ are site-independent.

nodes.name: First-order correction: Onsager term
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, inserting $f^{\prime}(K_{\mu \to i}) \simeq f^{\prime}(K_\mu-\Phi_{\mu i}\hat{x}_i) \simeq f^{\prime}(K_\mu)-\Phi_{\mu i} f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \hat{x}_i$ and $g^{\prime}(H_{i \to \mu}) \simeq g^{\prime}(H_i+ \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu ) \simeq g^{\prime}(H_i)+\Phi_{\mu i} g^{\prime \prime}(H_i) \hat{a}_\mu$ into (\ref{RstepH}) and (\ref{RstepK}), respectively, yields
\begin{eqnarray}
H_i &\simeq&\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{B}\sum_{\mu=1}^M 
\Phi_{\mu i}^2 f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i \cr
&\simeq &\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{NB}\sum_{\mu=1}^M 
 f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i 
\cr
&=& \sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \Gamma \hat{x}_i \end{eqnarray}
and
\begin{eqnarray}
K_\mu &\simeq& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{A}\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i}^2 
g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr
&\simeq & \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{N A}\sum_{i=1}^N  
g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr
&=& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -B \hat{a}_\mu , \end{eqnarray}
where we set $\Gamma=(NB)^{-1}\sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu)$.
nodes.statement_short: First-order Taylor expansion of cavity fields yields the Onsager reaction term in $H_i$ and $-B\hat a_\mu$ in $K_\mu$.
